name: The Walters household at Wolf Point
head: walters_william

arrival.note: The year his tenancy begins in the succession, standing in for an arrival date.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says where this household came from

reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as tavern keeper, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.trade_reasons.lodging_and_victualling — the head's recorded trade is evidence about this household, and the draw it answered is the reason the record will carry until a source states one.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says why this household came, or a committed source that apportions the town's arrivals between the land sales, the canal and the harbour works

lives_at.note: A landlord lived in his house; the tenancy itself is the reconstructed part.

works_at.note: The Wolf Point house is the premises his tenancy is a tenancy OF, and a landlord's workplace is his house. Inferred rather than documented because the tenancy itself is the reconstructed part: the same body of sources that gives Walters the house from 1833 to 1836 also says the house stopped operating as a public house in 1834, so what he was doing here in July 1835 - if he was here - is open.

last_dated_appearance.note: NO SIGHTING, SO THE LEG IS A SOURCE'S SPAN. The card holds no dated reading of this person at or before the scene date; the date here is the far end of what a cited source COVERS, which the role's own note calls the source's bound and not the man's. Read from `roles[] (source_span)` as `1673/1871`, which reaches 1871-12-31 — a window that covers 1835-07-01 itself, so it pins no last sighting before the day and cannot be read as one. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: If the house had closed as a public house in 1834, what Walters was doing at Wolf Point in July 1835 - or whether he was there - is open.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

ruling.what_happened: DRAWN, AND ORDERED BY A RULING RATHER THAN BY THE QUOTA. The household model drew this house married at 3 and the order book had no woman left in the wife's cell, and no woman the town already holds fits it. T-2021 ruled that houses like this are given the whole family the model drew for them, in a seeded order, while the town the book converges to stays at or under 3,265 people and its under-ten share inside the town model's bracket; this house came 114 of 277 in that order, before the walk stopped. The 2 kin seated here are the very ones this stage drew for it, by the same seeds: no source names any of them, and none says this man married.

occupation.note: The building record's operator succession gives Walters the Wolf Point house from 1833 to 1836, which covers the scene date.

persons.note: DERIVED, AND THE REASON IS A CONTRADICTION IN THE SOURCES RATHER THAN A GAP. The same body of material that puts Walters in the house 1833-1836 also says the house stopped operating as a public house in 1834, and a landlord of a closed house is not a coherent claim. data/structures/wolf_point_tavern.json records the occupancy as inferred for exactly this reason; this household inherits the doubt and does not paper over it.

resident_research.evidence_for: Andreas-derived Wolf Point history gives William Walters as proprietor of the Wolf Point Tavern from 1833 through 1836. That strongly supports scene-period continuity, but because it is a retrospective year range rather than a July 1 instrument the household's cautious presence flag is not silently upgraded here.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254. A CORROBORATOR, NOT A SECOND FOUNDATION (T-1254): drloih_wolf_point corroborates this role and is deliberately absent from the person's own `sources[]`, which lists what the 1835 RESIDENCY grade stands on. A volume that speaks to the trade and not to the residence does not join it.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 20 under 30', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('walters_william:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: THE WEST BANK'S OLDEST PUBLIC HOUSE AND ITS LEAST CERTAIN OCCUPANT. This household is written so that the west-bank row is not left as buildings with nobody in them, and it is graded derived throughout because the sources behind it contradict each other about whether there was a tavern here to keep. THE SUCCESSION THIS RECORD SITS AT THE END OF is worth keeping in view for the derived phase: Archibald Caldwell for James Kinzie by 1829, Elijah 'Old Geese' Wentworth from early 1830, Charles and Mary Taylor 1831-1833, then Walters. Four households this project has not written, three of them out of scope by date.
